newsitem.title: SPAIN: GOLF-JAMES BOOSTS RYDER CUP HOPES WITH SUDDEN-DEATH WIN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-JAMES BOOSTS RYDER CUP HOPES WITH SUDDEN-DEATH WIN.

text.p: Englishman Mark James kept alive his hopes of a Ryder Cup place when he beat Greg Norman at the third hole of a sudden-death playoff at La Moreleja to win the Spanish Open on Sunday.
James, who won the event in 1988, collected the $135,000 first prize with a par at the third extra hole, his final-hole bogey and Norman's 25-feet birdie putt having forced the shoot-out.
Both had finished on 11-under-par 277 with James, who started the final day one behind Norman, closing with a three-under-par 69 to the Australian's 70.
Norman appeared to have blown his chances when he bogeyed the short 17th for the first time in the day to fall two shots behind the Englishman.
But then James missed from five feet to drop a stroke on the last and then watched in dismay as the Australian sank his birdie putt on the last.

At the first extra hole, Norman, who lost his number one world ranking last week after 96 weeks on top, was in perfect place on the fairway but pulled his shot into a bunker and could only pitch out to 10 feet.
James drove into scrub but produced a fine second shot and comfortably made his par.
They could not be separated at the second sudden-death hole either but on the third - the short 17th - Norman came up short with his tee shot, chipped short and ran the putt past the hole.
James ran an approach putt up from 40 feet and tapped in for his 24th victory worldwide and his first since he took the Moroccan Open in 1995.
It also moved him up to 18th in the European Order of Merit and kick-started his bid for an eighth Ryder Cup place against the United States in September.

"This means a lot for me and for me to putt this well was quite miraculous. I am really turning around my game after a bad spell and now I have an outside chance of at least threatening for a Ryder Cup spot," said James.
"I treated the play-off just like normal stroke play hoping he'd make a mess-up and I got lucky when he did. But they were tough play-off holes and anyone could have done that."
For Norman, it meant a second shoot-out defeat on the European tour in two months, having lost out, along with Welshman Ian Woosnam, to fellow-Australian Richard Green in the Desert Classic in Dubai.
"I played very good but the ball just didn't want to go the way I wanted it," said Norman.
Eduardo Romero of Argentina birdied the last for a share of third place with Sweden's Jarmo Sandlein, who came through the field with a 66, the joint-best round of the week.
